fields.h1: Build Game Survey Questions and Act on the Answers
fields.hero_description: Build game survey questions for playtests, game nights, and party games, with every answer saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Game Survey Built by Emergent Handles
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the questions and the app that runs them, with skip logic and an alert when a result crosses your line.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted for your game

Describe the game, the players, and the decision the answers feed. Emergent drafts the rating, ranking, and open questions, and a follow-up prompt rewrites any one of them.
fields.feature_2:
Questions that follow the player

The survey branches on earlier answers. A tester who quit at level 6 skips every question about level 10 and rates only the levels they played, with no blank rows to clean up.
fields.feature_3:
One question per screen on a phone

Players answer one question per screen on a phone, between rounds or on the bus home. A difficulty rating is a single tap, and an open answer gets a full-width text box.
fields.feature_4:
Answers tagged by build or session

Every response is a row in a database you own, tagged with the build number or the session date. Compare level 9 on build 14 with build 15 without merging two spreadsheets.
fields.feature_5:
An alert when a threshold is crossed

Set a threshold, such as half the testers rating a level 5 for difficulty. The designer gets a Slack or email alert when it is crossed, with the level and the count.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, your code, no response cap

Host the survey on your own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. Responses have no cap, and on paid plans the full code exports to your GitHub repository.

fields.tab_content_1:
Level 9 gets 3 more moves after 34 testers call it too hard

Quillbright Games sends a playtest survey to the 60 testers of Reefshine, its tile-matching puzzle game. Each tester rates every level they reached on a 5-point difficulty scale. Of the 52 who answer, 34 rate level 9 a 5. The designer adds 3 moves to level 9 before the next build goes out.
fields.tab_content_2:
The cafe gives its Thursdays to co-op games

Rollhaven Board Game Cafe has a free night each week and no plan for it. Its survey asks which night each member comes in and which kind of game they reach for first. It goes to 140 members, and 96 answer. Of those, 44 pick Thursday, and co-op games lead with 38 votes. Thursday becomes co-op night.
fields.tab_content_3:
Exploration ranked first before the campaign starts

Five players sit down for the first Ember Hollow session on Friday. The game master's session zero survey has each player rank combat, roleplay, and exploration, then list topics to keep out of the game, saved without names. Exploration comes first for 4 of 5 players, so the first arc is mapping a sunken city.
fields.tab_content_4:
A party game board written by 84 coworkers

A week before the Wexmoor Supply holiday party, 84 staff answer 8 open questions, such as something people forget at the office. The host merges near matches like charger and phone charger. The top 5 answers to each question go on the game board, and phone charger leads with 29 of 84.

Count the votes for each night and each kind of game, and show me the top night and the top kind.", sessionZero: "Build a session zero survey for my tabletop group of 5 players. faq_plan.q: How do I create game survey questions?

plan.angle: The top 10 for game survey questions is a mix with no clear winner: Reddit and Facebook threads, a Scribd questionnaire about video game habits, a Survio template on video and board game habits, and a PlaytestCloud list of playtest questions for match-3 games, plus fan posts for survey-says style party games. None shows what the answers change. This page covers the four jobs searchers mean (a playtest, a player habits survey, a tabletop session zero survey, and a survey-says party game built from real answers) and shows each one ending in a decision, with question advice in the how-to and FAQ.
tab_stories: Quillbright Games sends a playtest survey to 60 testers of its match-3 game Reefshine; 52 answer, 34 of 52 rate level 9 a 5 out of 5 for difficulty, and the designer adds 3 moves to level 9 before the next build.

Before the first session of the Ember Hollow campaign, the game master asks 5 players to rank combat, roleplay, and exploration and to list topics to keep out of the game; 4 of 5 rank exploration first, and the first arc becomes mapping a sunken city.

A week before the Wexmoor Supply holiday party, 84 staff answer 8 open questions; the host merges near matches, the top 5 answers per question go on the game board, and phone charger leads one question with 29 of 84.
